article.title: Burkina Faso: Thomas Sankara, the cut-short revolution, and the legacy of feminism
article.author: Editor
article.content: The original distinctiveness of Sankarist thought lies in having simultaneously attacked three pillars of structural oppression: imperialist dependence, through the outright rejection of international public debt, defined as a “neocolonial instrument of reconquest and the economic assassination of peoples”; the internal class structure and bureaucratic rent, through the dismantling of the privileges of the parasitic state bourgeoisie—nourished by French aid funds and disconnected from the material needs of the peasant masses; and patriarchal oppression. The post Burkina Faso: Thomas Sankara, the cut-short revolution, and the legacy of feminism appeared first on MR Online .
